items.originalTitle: Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts general availability

en.title: Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts general availability
en.summary: Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts is now generally available.
en.details:
Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts is now generally available. It remediates alerts by working across your codebase the way a developer would: it explores relevant files, proposes a fix, and reruns CodeQL to confirm the fix closes the alert before opening a pull request for your review. Agentic autofix is available to GitHub Code Security and GitHub Advanced Security customers on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, including GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency.

How it works

When you assign a code scanning alert to Copilot, it:

- Explores relevant files across your codebase.

- Generates a proposed fix.

- Validates the fix works by rerunning CodeQL.

- Iterates if needed, then opens a draft pull request ready for your review.

The pull request includes a summary of the fix, why it closes the alert, and the validation steps Copilot took to confirm that it works. When the pull request containing the fix is ready, you can instruct Copilot to make further changes to it by commenting on the pull request or interacting with the session in the Agents tab of your repository.

How to use it

When enabled, agentic autofix replaces the free Generate Fix option on individual code scanning alerts with an Assign to Copilot button.

You can use agentic autofix:

- From any code scanning alert on the repository’s default branch, by assigning the alert to Copilot. …

en.details:
Much of today’s scientific progress begins with computation.

But turning accelerated computing’s potential into scientific progress — modeling climate systems, designing molecules, simulating materials and more — depends on more than breakthrough technology. Especially for smaller labs, early-career scientists or science-based startups, the hardest part of research can be everything that comes before the science: assembling tools, finding compute and building the expertise to use both.

At the AI in Science Summit in Dublin today, the European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative, a shared framework connected to RAISE — the Resource for AI Science in Europe — that brings private-sector support closer to Europe’s research community.

Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

NVIDIA is joining the campaign , providing:

- Access to accelerated tools, models and platforms

- Compute, cloud resources, data and scientific resources

- Skills, training and technical support

- Collaborative projects and pilots along with support for researchers and talent

- Support for startups and ecosystem development …

en.title: More Than Three Quarters of Small Business Owners Say AI Makes Them More Productive, But Most Need More Guidance
en.summary: Today, we’re releasing findings from a new YouGov study we commissioned of almost 4,000 small business owners across nine APAC markets: Australia, Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, Taiwan, India, Thailand, Japan and Hong Kong, on how AI is …
en.details:
Today, we’re releasing findings from a new YouGov study we commissioned of almost 4,000 small business owners across nine APAC markets: Australia, Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, Taiwan, India, Thailand, Japan and Hong Kong, on how AI is helping them grow, compete with larger businesses and reach customers beyond their borders.

AI adoption is already broad, with 84% of surveyed small business owners currently using AI, 76% reporting a positive impact on productivity and 71% reporting a positive impact on revenue or sales over the past 12 months. Small business owners also report AI helps tackle two significant challenges facing small businesses: limited resources and limited time.

- Owners say AI is helping small businesses compete. Across the nine markets, four in five (80%) owners agree AI helps small businesses compete more effectively with larger companies, and the same proportion say it makes starting a business easier. 83% agree AI enables small businesses to do things that previously required significantly more money or resources.

- And, they say the time saved is going back into the business. Among those reporting a positive productivity impact from using AI, 58% are using the time to improve the quality of their existing work, 50% are putting it into growth and business planning, and 46% are getting more done with the team they already have. …
